title: My brain needs Brain.fm daily to focus
body:
If you have a neurodivergent brain, this app is a lifesaver! 

For work, I listen to "Deep Focus" on my desktop computer every single day when I have to lock in and accomplish my tasks. In total silence, my brain goes off on tangents, but when I use brain.FM, it occupies the "wandering" or distracted part of my brain with non-lyric, interesting, non-repetitive looping jams so I can actually get things done.

For household tasks, or if I'm having trouble getting moving in the mornings, I use the "Motivation" music, and for whatever reason, it gets my toes tapping and helps me tidy, declutter, and finish chores with no struggling.

When I'm anxious or getting ready for a presentation or event, I listen to "Destress" while I'm preparing to calm my nerves.

At night, I listen to "Wind Down" or "Deep Sleep" to relax before bed.

Right now I'm on an 86-week streak of using this app in so many settings of my life, and I truly couldn't function without it. I recommend it to everyone I know who has ADHD or focus issues – it's exactly what I need to get things done!

body: Interesting backend science, weak frontend empathy” is probably the best short description of Brain.fm. I like the concept… not the very simple and limited user experience.

title: Definitely helps my ADHD focus issues at least a bit!
body:
This app hasn’t been a transformative, life-changing discovery like some ads suggest, but I’ve been using it for over half a year now and I definitely notice some improvement in my focus and attention when using it! Exactly how much of a difference depends on the day/time/circumstances, but it’s enough that this has become a regular ADHD management tool for me, for everything from studying to working on creative projects, really anything that I need a focus boost for. 

The most significant improvement for me happens when my brain is hitting that boredom-burnout point on long assignments or study sessions. Putting on the music in this app helps get my brain out of the disengaged/distracted slump, or at least reduces how bad it is. If I was already having a relatively good focus day I don’t notice as much impact; I’m sure there’s still at least little, but it’s less obvious. 

As a side note, I’m really glad the app has the thumbs down button permanently skip songs. I have some misophonia and there have been several songs that had just the wrong combination of sounds in order to trigger it, but being able to simply remove those songs from rotation means that’s not a serious problem. 

I do wish there was a way to have playlists in addition to the favorites library though…

author: Lucasnad27

title: Theres A Critical Flaw
body:
Personally, I find it remarkably short-sighted on the part of the marketing and development teams to take such a low-resolution risk. I always appreciate a preliminary trial period—it’s a necessary means of developing initial rapport with an app. However, the experience within that trial is everything.

While the content itself is lovely and the interface reasonably well-organized, the experience is undermined by what feels like an overly aggressive sales tactic. Each time the app is reopened, users are met with a full-page subscription prompt—effectively shouting “BUY, BUY, BUY” in their faces. It’s not only excessive; it’s uncomfortable. Literally every time you close or switch between apps, you’re forced to navigate through this.

I have no objection to a business earning revenue, but how you go about it reveals what truly motivates you. If user experience is so readily disrupted by profit-driven interruptions, then user wellbeing clearly isn’t the priority. The focus, quite plainly, is on maximizing subscriptions. If that weren’t the case, this constant paywall push wouldn’t exist—or at least would be more thoughtfully implemented. And that isn’t actually the issue; profit is critical, obviously. But this is a poor strategy, considering how simple of a mistake it is. I promise—regardless of what statistics you’re using—this is a low-resolution mistake aimed at short-term gain, not long-term success.

And that leads me to the core concern: if I can’t trust the intent behind your methods, how can I trust the integrity of your content? I’ve enjoyed the music, and I think there’s real potential within the model itself—the app has even complemented my workflow—but it’s difficult to fully invest in something that treats trust as secondary to conversion rates, and does so so casually and carelessly. You could have at least hidden the intent to some degree—or at all.

You could do better—and frankly, you should want to.

author: Dr. Charmer

title: Never Rated an App Before
body: So I’ve been really struggling with focus issues at work. It started about a year and half ago. I’ve tried brain supplements and drinks for focus. Nootropics and even something called Thesis. But for some reason none of it has worked on me. However when I put on my sound cancelling over ear headphones, and turn on brain.fm I’m so locked in. It’s weird how well it works. I don’t know if it’s a gimmick that neuroscientists actually mimic the brainwaves for focus in the music, but the fact is the outcome is it works. I’ve used YouTube focus music and sometimes that works but brain.fm works everytime. Sometimes I notice I procrastinate by not putting on my headphones to turn on some brain.fm cause I’m convinced I’ll do work when I put it on. Honestly I’ve used screen time apps too and they’re not nearly as helpful as brain.fm. The yearly membership is pretty affordable which I’m getting after my monthly runs out.

author: Vivian🩵⚡️

title: NOT FOR ALERT JOBS and maladaptive daydreamers
body:
I work at a doggy daycare my job goes from fast to slow and i need to be alert I’m on ADHD meds and I still zone out into another world. I put it on my headphones set it to focus deep work and started watching my dogs. 

I zoned out faster then normal and stayed zoned out until a coworker called my name on the walkie. I came to with dogs playing crazily! 

This app dulls your senses it might be great for office work or a job that is rhythmic but if your job requires you to be alert and aware such as fast food, operating heavy machinery, any work with kids or animals, being on an active construction zone. Ect. This is not the app for you! 

Worst part was after the music my alert senses were COMPLETELY GONE THE WHOLE DAY!

This app does work but it’s not going to enhance your awareness it’s going to reduce it!!!!

If you are prone to daydreaming or getting lost in thought DO NOT USE THIS APP IN A MOMENT YOU NEED TO BE ALERT IN! 

I’m going home now and use this app to zone out and get things done hopefully. 

Great app. Not what I was expecting.

author: StormBlessed SunEater

title: Helps my ADHD and PTSD symptoms.
body: I love that the app asks if I have ADHD because that means the music should be different. I have tried listening to “calming music” before but always got irritated or bored. Brain.fm suggested I use high neural effect and it helps immensely with my ADHD. I can put on high neural effect Motivation or Light Tasks to help me get things done. Podcasts are good sometimes but no lyric music is sometimes the exact thing that I need. I can put on chill or destress to help calm after a panicky moment. I listen to Deep Sleep all night. My EMDR therapist recognized that it is an effective tool to help me through transition times and difficult moods. I listen to Learning after an EMDR session and I feel that the bilateral music supports me in that nebulous transition from therapy to the present. Or I listen to Motivation after a talk session and it helps me feel like I can conquer whatever comes next and helps me to focus on the present moment.

title: Sleep & Focus Improvement
body:
I have struggled with sleep for years, and I would wake up multiple times a night. That changed within the first week of using the sleep feature within this app. The music and waves stimulate my brain in a way that I can’t explain but it works. If you can improve your rest, even slightly over time, you can improve your life when you are awake tenfold. The focus feature is also great for keeping my brain engaged and maintained with whatever project I am tackling. The timer is so great. I love to look up while I’m working to see how long I’ve been at it and I don’t have to click on my phone to have the chance to get distracted. 
Lastly, the only downfall for me is that the price is a bit out of my budget but they give you a long time for a free trial. The YouTuber Mark Manson recommended BrainFM in one of his videos and I’ve loved it ever since. Give it a try, your brain will thank you! 😄

title: Everything  and more
body:
This app has exceeded my expectations.  I originally bought it for my son, who is a convert to this concept, to help him focus during studies. I decided to try it out because other apps have failed when it comes to helping me stay asleep at night. 

I can’t believe how many more hours of sleep I’m getting in the deep sleep mode.  Waking upon tossing and turning used to mean I couldn’t go back to sleep for an hour or two.   I also have been using it during waking hours to be energized upon getting out of bed. 

Functionalities in this app don’t even compare to other sleep apps that I’ve used. I didn’t realize how much I would love, as my son does, to be able to create a library of music specific to my particular taste in genres for certain modes.  But that’s just the icing on the cake.   Most people would likely be satisfied with just simply liking or disliking a particular track that the program chooses for you based on the ‘task’ you’re choosing.

I’ve turned a friend on to this app who has trouble falling asleep and she raves about that functionality.    Love, love, love!!!

body:

I like how it lets you easily skip to another track if the one being offered to you isn’t helpful / too distracting.
I love the deep work option and I’ve tried the section to help with sleep- but the deep work (inside the focus section) is the best. 
My noise canceling headphones died so I’ve been just playing this through my phone speakers- even then it still works (although I prefer the headphones- after I’ve been listening to anything on brain FM while wearing headphones as soon as I take them off, there is a noticeable “pop” in my ears- like I’ve just changed altitude)
A friend of mine had a headache and this app helped lessen its intensity. If you want a shortcut into flow state, then brain.fm is your friend. Worth the money!

title: Better than
body:
I’m 23 weeks in using this app and it is my most important tool. I came to brain.fm for the variety and I stayed because I found I can actually focus. 

I’ve tried several things to calm my monkey mind and give it something to occupy itself with while I work, read or plan. I’ve had a waterfall on my desk physically and monitor virtually , I’ve listened to classical music (thank you Mozart), I’ve listened to white noise, tried brown noise, and I even bought an album with nothing but the sounds of a coffee shop (a favorite by the way) I’ve listened to more audiobooks than I can count(for the more repetitive tasks).  I’ve even tried working on my computer in VR to shut out distractions (how much battery do I have left?)

I tried brain.fm because the coffee shop was getting old but I’ve found that (coupled with noise canceling headphones or even regular earbuds), I can sit at the kitchen table in the middle of life happening and still focus on what I’m doing.  Where my wife walking by used to throw me off, now I barely notice.  It’s almost like VR. I’ve also been attacking my distractibility from other angles but, I was using brain.fm before that. 

As I’ve used it I gradually added in or took away certain sounds. I’ve liked what I liked and thumb downed what I didn’t (the evil drone didn’t work for me) I’ve done the meditation, I tried sleep but it pulled a Pink Floyd Dark Side of the Moon and scared me awake after lulling me off, easily fixable with a thumb down. 

Thank you guys for a great app and the work you’ve put into it. If the science is just a scam don’t tell me about it because it’s been working great for me.  I suspect there has to be something to the science though because every now and then I stop and realize “I’ve been working on this for 2 hours?”

title: Skeptical at first but now sold
body:
I have ADHD and suffer from severe difficulty focusing on a frequent basis. I’m also musically inclined so listening to normal music in the background is usually more distracting than helpful. I had heard trusted influencers recommend Brain.fm but I was skeptical at first because I already pay for music subscriptions and macOS and iOS come with native sounds of nature you can play on repeat so it seemed like I should be able to get by without spending more money, especially when it’s a significant amount. I tried looking up the research to see if it was legit studies proving the music actually helps someone focus and my attempts were inconclusive.

Nevertheless, I tried the trial and noticed an immediate difference in my ability to focus. The music is not distracting but just fades into the background. I was also afraid it wouldn’t have enough diversity of music or genres to choose from but they actually have a ton of diversity and are continuously coming out with new tracks. I try new stuff all the time and haven’t yet heard it all. I also expanded to the other types of music, for meditation and for sleeping, when needed. Sometimes I get a little craving for real music in the background but I still want the cognitive effects of brain.fm so I will layer it by playing it from the brain.fm website a little softer volume than my Apple Music while I’m working and this works well.

There of course is no magic bullet for ADHD but I have been using it for 30 straight weeks now and I believe it is an indispensable tool in my arsenal for treating ADHD without medication.

title: Amazing app, good science
body:
When I was younger, I worked with my psychiatrist grandfather, using EEG Neuro-biofeedback to train children with ADHD to avoid symptoms without use of stimulant medication‘s. 

We had great success teaching their brains through simple games and an EEG interface. This training allowed suffering children - who were addicted to stimulant medication’s - to control their own brains, electrical activity, on command, moving them from the lower electrical pattern states to the sensory motor rhythm (SMR) and beta ranges that are necessary for normal life and focused work. 

It was all the more effective at reducing hyperactivity, which is a shiver response. The brain unconsciously triggers ‘hyperactivity’ when it recognizes it’s electrical activity is insufficient for the tasks it is being asked to perform. 

Now, why do I tell you all of this? 

Because this app uses essentially the same technology, training your brain via entrainment to self recognize and self regulate the electrical patterns in your brain necessary to maintain focus. This applies equally to relaxation, to sleep, and everything else in your life. 

This app is amazing, and I strongly recommended it to anyone, regardless of perceived need or real experience. This app works, and the science is real. Give it a chance and you’ll see for yourself.

I get they have their core product and should and likely understand and know their product better than the market, but how can you tell a customer that has a need their product can meet, and for good reason, then tell their customer their idea or need doesn’t have merit. title: Just amazing!
body:
I recently had a chance to try out both Brain.fm and Endel, two apps that claim to improve sleep and energy levels through music and soundscapes. My experience with both apps was quite different, and I have to say that Brain.fm stood out as the clear winner.

For the past few months, I had been feeling horrible no matter how much sleep I got. Desperate for a solution, I decided to give Brain.fm a try with their one-week trial. I was amazed by the results. Every night I used Brain.fm, I would wake up feeling tired as usual, but in the middle of the day, I would get a sudden boost of energy. It was a noticeable difference that helped me power through the rest of the day with more focus and alertness.

Encouraged by the results with Brain.fm, I decided to give Endel a try, as it claimed to be a similar app at a lower cost. However, my experience with Endel was disappointing. I used the app for two nights, and each day I woke up feeling even more drained and worse than before. I could barely make it through the day without feeling fatigued and sluggish. It was clear that Endel was not delivering the promised benefits for me, and I had to discontinue using it for the remainder of the trial.

In conclusion, I found Brain.fm to be a more effective and reliable option for improving my sleep and energy levels. While it may be a bit more expensive compared to Endel, the results were worth it for me. Brain.fm actually delivered on its promises, while Endel felt like a gimmick that didn't provide the desired benefits. I highly recommend giving Brain.fm a try if you're looking for an app to enhance your sleep and energy levels. It's been a game-changer for me, and I plan to continue using it to maintain my improved sleep and daytime productivity. Don't waste your time and money on cheaper alternatives like Endel, go for the real deal with Brain.fm! 5/5 stars. Overall, I highly recommend Brain.fm for anyone seeking to improve their sleep and energy levels through music and soundscapes. It may be slightly more expensive than some other options, but the results are well worth it. Say goodbye to fatigue and hello to renewed energy with Brain.fm!

title: Sleep tracks & focus work really well for me
body:
2023 update: After using this app for years, I am removing my five star review. This app has become unusable. It crashes dozens of times each night when I’m ready to play the sleep tracks. The logo screen loads for a few seconds and then the whole app shuts down… over and over. Sometimes I can get it to finally load and it will function, other times it will crash in the middle of the night and wake me up. Most of the time in recent weeks, I can’t get the app to function at all.

When the app works, there are some other problems: 

I haven’t been able to get the downloaded tracks to work offline at all. 

I miss the nap feature or an option to select a shorter sleep period.

The streak feature is utterly pointless.

I mostly use the sleep tracks, but if use the focus tracks more if I could stream them from my MacBook while working. I’ve had major problems in recent years: track will stop, infinity won’t work, or I won’t be able to play it at all. I’d use my phone instead, but now the app crashes all the time.

It’s such a shame because the tracks really are great. 

Original review:

I’ve used earbuds & an ocean soundtrack at night for years due to my snoring husband. I switched to brain.fm a couple of months ago after I broke my leg in a bad accident and started having PTSD. I had been using brain.fm focus tracks for work, and was pleased with the results. The sleep tracks work really well for me. I only have a few small complaints: I don’t like keeping my phone connected to WiFi & the cell tower all night. I wish I could download 10-12 hours for use offline. This would also help should the cell service and/or WiFi go down as both sometimes do. I would also wish to eliminate the brief pause between sleep tracks. This small silence sometimes wakes me up which is bothersome as it takes me a long time to fall back to sleep. I have not had any connectivity issues.

title: This is my secret weapon
body:
EDIT: it’s just about to turn 2023 and I still use this every day and night. Absolutely one of the best app purchases I’ve ever made, and definitely one of the most frequently used, especially considering that it’s not a primary tool or anything. Working, resting, traveling, sleeping… Brain.fm has something for all occasions. And they just keep making it better… So excellent, much wow.

I’ve had a lifetime brain.fm subscription since 2015, and have never regretted it for even a second. I use it for sleep, I use it for focus, I use it for general relaxation throughout the day, it is a phenomenal tool. I recommend it to absolutely anyone who will listen and if used properly, it can literally give you more time in your day. One of the ways in which I use this service, is to help me achieve “polyphasic sleeping“. With the app’s help, I have trained my brain to be able to hit REM sleep within 5 to 10 minutes, which means I can take a 30 or 45 minute “power nap” using Brain.fm, and when I come out of it I feel like I’ve just had at least three or four hours of sleep. I can then go on to function for easily 2 to 4 more hours at optimal functionality before I begin to feel at all tired. From time to time I like to pull “all nighters“ by using this technique to take a short 15-30 minute nap every two or three hours. When I am feeling in the zone coding, or writing, or doing any sort of focus work, this is absolutely priceless. I also almost always use this during the day when I am working, as the focus music selections are tremendously varied and I never get tired of them. Lately I have been exploring some of the other music categories I had ignored for years, and they have added so much content to all the different areas, there is just a huge selection of music now to suit any mood. So to sum up, brain.fm is my secret productivity weapon, both squeezing more out of my working life, but also literally giving me more waking hours in the day. What’s that worth? I can’t even begin to put a dollar price on it.

author: brain.am

title: Used-frustrated-now using again
body:
I used this app when it first came out. (Two years ago? More?) I experienced some of the glitches that were talked about in other reviews. Music not downloading. Timer was “wonky”. Loading issues where the app randomly crashes or freezes. 

The last four months or so, this is a completely new app from the when it began. It absolutely works and works like you would expect any app to work. 

The most unexpected surprise came with selecting the genre. One of the Meditation tracks had a bird that kind of triggered my misophonia. So, I just switched to bells and chimes. Magic. 

The Focus tracks absolutely blow me away. It’s like taking a supplement but without the weird side effects and issues that come with those. I haven’t deliberately lost track of time while working on something (writing) since my late twenties.

I’m retired now and never thought I would be as distracted as I am but I’ve allowed myself to fall into the distraction minefield that is todays landscape. This app is a potent antidote to that. 

If I were picking nits, I would ask for the timer to not reset completely when switching genres. Or maybe the option to customize the time. But that’s not really an issue. I just set an alarm on phone, ipad, watch or desk clock (if I need to limit my time) and I’m good to go.

I recently heard the developers on a podcast from a while ago and how they are using their own product. That’s a comfort. Hopefully this app continues to improve. 

One thing that would be an interesting solve is for the Sleep tracks. I can’t use headphones when I sleep. Just doesn’t work.  So my workaround has been to use the Sleep tracks before laying down and then just kind of sliding off to sleep. Not a big deal. I’ve thought about setting up a dual-speaker set up above my head in the bed, but it’s not enough of an issue to get into all of that. 

Thanks developers and everyone who made this app happen and brought it up to snuff.

title: Missing key features to make it 5-stars
body:
Firstly, the music in this app is genuinely great! I love the variance in it, and I love that you can adjust the intensity depending on your scenario. But for the price of the subscription, they really need to add some features to make it a truly 5-stars experience.

1) Background play. Let me play another audio source from another app overtop Brain.fm. It’s one of my favorite features from other ambient music and sound apps. I like to be able to listen to an audio book while hearing focus music, or an asmr youtube video while still hearing sleep/relax music.

2) Home screen widgets for quickly jumping into the different kinds of music. Seems like a no-brainer.

3) Siri shortcuts. This one is HUGE! I use Brain.fm for sleep music nearly every night. It would be amazing if I could have a shortcut that jumped right into the exact type of sleep music I want at the exact volume I want without having to navigate the app itself. Other ambient music apps do this, and it’s a killer feature for me. When I’m sleepy, I don’t want to jump through a lot of hoops to get my music setup.

4) Integration with Apple Health. This is a minor one, but since Brain.fm offers meditation music and guides, it would be nice if mindfulness could be logged into Apple Health, potentially also keeping track of my heart rate and breath rate.

5) Fade between songs. This is a real small one, but sometimes I feel like there’s a harsh cut between songs and it’s a little jarring. Just have the tracks cross fade for a second or two when I’m changing tunes.

Other suggestions I have are things like a standalone Apple Watch app, music for walking, running, and exercising in general, and an option to automatically download songs you’ve liked so they’re available offline.

I feel like the app right now is polished for what it is. The music is great and the navigation is intuitive. It just needs more features for the price of the subscription. Hope the devs read this and take at least some of what I suggest into account.

title: Love this service but there are some annoyances
body:
I found out about this service a couple of years ago via review articles from mainstream media. I was skeptical and tried it out. I was converted immediately. It simply works for me. I only use it to focus on work and there is something magical about those binaural beats. The subscription fee is a little steep but I need this so I am still a subscriber. I hope the developers are listening because I have a few annoyances I wish they would fix. I saw a previous review that covered the issues with downloading music. I understand this is fixed in an upcoming update which is wonderful to hear. It’s just so annoying to wait a few seconds for each song to play. Along the same lines, the app takes too long to startup. Also, If I’m listening to a song and I get interrupted by another app or phone call, it doesn’t continue playing after the interruption. The app doesn’t seem to be persistent enough. I also find that the same songs play over and over and in the same order. It would be nice if they played in a random fashion. Also, given this is a subscription, I assumed new music would be introduced more regularly. Maybe it is and I am completely missing it. Not sure but these annoyances have made me look elsewhere at other services. I hope these things get fixed soon so that I can continue to be a satisfied subscriber.

UPDATE (May 12, 2022)
Brain.fm developers, things have improved a little since my last review. However, I kept hearing there was a major update in the works and have not seen anything since. I still hope it’s coming. Also, please add settings to set default option or at least remember last duration and neural effect filter level. I only use >Focus>Deep Work which is ok to tap through. Except I have then change duration and neural effect every time. Would be really helpful to just come in and have alone tap to start my fav options. Thanks.

title: (Some) Great music, horrible user experience
body:
I eventually canceled my subscription.

There are some factors that made me stop using the app. But before listing what I hated about the app, I would like to say that I really liked some music.

Here are some reasons that made me hate the app. 

1. Lack of custom settings
I liked certain genres, such as grooves, lofi, and electronic (in case of "focus"). For some reason, on the other hand, I really hated most of the natural sounds. There is no way I can listen to a certain set of genres, it's either choosing one or all. I ended up keeping changing from grooves to lofi to electronics, etc.
Also, I usually use "infinity". However, because 90 minutes is the default and there is no way to customize it, I always have to go extra steps to change the time.   

2. No way to keep playing without interacting with the app
Sometimes I focus intensely on something, and the music definitely helps. Then the music ends, because 90 minutes have passed. I don't want my focus to be disturbed, so I click the play button in the lock screen, and nothing happens. I realize that I have to go back to the app, click "x" on the pop-up saying congratulations, then click "focus" again, click "infinity" again, click "deep work" again, click the genre button again, and finally click "grooves" again. My focus is already disturbed.

3. Limited number of music
My favorite genre is "Grooves". But there are only two groovy songs in the entire Relax category (in "Chill"). "Lofi" doesn't exist at all. 
There are many songs in "Electronic", but many of those in Relax category are somewhat depressing (although "Stratosphere" and "Highway Lights" are my two favorites in this app, I will miss these two pieces).         

In conclusion, some music in Brain.fm was really good, to the point I listened to them not just for practical reasons but for pure entertainment. I will probably miss them. However, the user experience was way too horrible.

title: Great way to relax or focus
body:
I've been using brain.fm for years, and I don't know what secret sauce powers their magical music, but IT WORKS FOR ME. I have ADHD, so sometimes finding focus is a bit like looking for a needle in a haystack. 

But where generic "background noise" apps can actually end up distracting me more, brain.fm actually has such a wide array of sounds that my brain actually does what I want it to do: whether that's focus on a creative writing project, relax enough for a nap (especially difficult with third trimester insomnia, so thank you, brain.fm, for helping me get ANY sleep!), or do deep work, brain.fm helps me do it all.

If there's ever a sound/track I don't like (did I mention I also have aural synesthesia and some sounds make me feel REALLY weird?), I can easily switch to something different with a tap; there's such a variety of tracks for each mental state. You can even browse their extensive library if you're not sure which mental state seems right for the moment. You can even save favorites for offline use, if you're say, traveling and won't have a constant data connection.

All in all, a fantastic app that I love using, mostly for focus, but great for meditation, relaxation, and falling asleep.
author: MeredithSS

title: Brain.fm pushes my work into overdrive!
body:
I’ve always relied on music to help me remain more focused as I am working, so I’m less distracted, to give me energy, and to dampen the sounds around me. One day, I was listening to the 5AM Miracle podcast and Jeff Sanders (#398) interviewed Dan Clark, CEO of Brain.fm and I’ve had a 398 day ever since! It literally changed my way of working. 

I’ve gotten into the zone more quickly and remained in the sound longer with Brain.fm versus just relying on music I select from my music sources. I’ve made my office time more efficient by remaining on task longer, and staying deeper into thought while completing more focused work. 

What’s more, Brain.fm has been so supportive in assisting ajd answering questions! Talk about high ranking customer service! In fact, getting up and starting off my 5AM morning routine, I sent an email to Brain.fm asking a question and shouldn’t have been shocked that not long after I received a reply (not just a template response saying someone would be in touch, a really person reaching out to provide guidance and information!). 

It’s made such a world of difference in my productivity levels, I’ve added the link to their trial subscription to both my emails (personal and professional) signature lines to encourage colleagues, friends, and family to join, because it’s made that much difference in how productive it’s made me - and my systems and flow were already pretty darn good! 

Speaking of subscriptions, Brain.fm offers a lower end price both monthly or full year, all for less than a coffeehouse coffee a week - It’s worth giving up one of those and easy to do because I’ve not relied as much on an afternoon coffee to keep me revved up because Brain.fm keeps me focused and energized without the caffeine. 

It’s been a LONG time since I’ve felt this excited about a product, but after doing some personal focus tests while working using Brain.fm and relying on my own music selections, hands down, Brain.fm is the winner. (I’m even buying a subscription for my brother and sister as Christmas gifts because they both work at computers doing intense jobs, and I believe Brain.fm will do for them what it already has done me).

Quality product, amazing support, effective results.

title: Missed opportunity: Doesn’t accommodate my ADHD
body:
With my ADHD, I don’t just have a hard time focusing. External structure and tools to help me maintain focus are important for me and many others with ADHD. Paradoxically, however, the more rigid that structure is, the more stifling and difficult to adhere to, and the more likely it will be to do more harm than good.

I thrive best under fluid structures and systems of time management. For example, I usually work on 25 minute intervals, but on some days, I may find that 7 minute or 3.5 minute intervals are what I need. I was dismayed to find that, not only was I not able to customize how long the timer was, but the five options I had to choose from were prohibitively long. Maintaining focus for 30 minutes is taxing. For 60 minutes? That requires herculean effort. At 90 minutes, I’d begin to lose focus every 30 seconds or so. And 120 minutes? Imagine how your brain would feel after reading the dictionary for six hours straight. That’s me after just two hours of any given office task.

Maybe this app wasn’t designed for my particular variant of ADHD. Maybe it wasn’t designed for ADHD people at all. That’s fine; neurotypical people need focus timer apps too. But I think that, since ADHD people are more likely than most to seek out focusing apps, designing your app to accommodate our challenges by allowing more flexibility and customizability may help a sizeable chunk of your user base.

author: mc22mc22

title: Best!
body: I’ve been using BrainFM for > 1.5yrs. and it has become totally indispensable.  My brain gets frazzled, fragmented, distractible, jittery and otherwise uncooperative when I’m tired, eating poorly, not moving.  It’s 200x worse when I’m stressed- my brain just won’t get and stay focused.  For me the relief is almost instant when I slip on the headphones (gotta be over the ear headphones for max efficacy.   Depending on the task and where my brain is at I’ll select the ‘Study & Read’ or the ‘Deep Work’ tracks under the ‘Focus’ menu. I’ll set the duration, eg 30 or 45min when I’m doing a series of ‘sprint’ study/ work sessions and when it stops I get up, move around etc then repeat.  Note: first time I put it on I started listening to the music to see if I’d like it I quickly realized however, that I don’t have to - it just works on me in the background.  Is it the same as just listening to songs or instrumentals? No comparison. That’d be like trying to determine the efficacy of Acetaminophen by the taste of the pill. The selling point for me is the almost immediate ‘ahhhhhhh!’ that my brain does when I use BrainFM.  Like someone stopped the fingernails down the blackboard. And quite a while later I truly am amazed when it dawns on me how long I’ve been hammering away at my work!  So it not only helps me transition into work, it maintains that state. If I’m in a noisy environment I just crank it up a little. But again, I really would recommend using w over the ear headphones for max benefits.   I know that’s long but I hope it helps you.

title: Excellent example how to degrade user experience by “over designing”
body:
I’ve been using the service/app since it was introduced - 2013? 2014? and each major design/app update makes it worse than it was. 

There are a lot of bugs/issues/“unnecessary features” was introduced lately with the major update,  but here is my favorite and most annoying, completely redesigned “session end” behavior which brings your frustration with the app to a next level:
1. Old app used to have a gentle fade at the end, now the sound just “stops in the middle”
2. Often you want to just continue the session after it finished - in older version, you just tap “play” on the phone screen,  or if the app is open,  in the session screen.  Now, you have to see stupid “congratulations” banner. Mind me asking “congratulations” with what?  Quite annoying to see it 5-6 times throughout the day in a past couple months.  And then you have to tap “go home”, select type of session, time  and tap play to continue, while it used to be just tap “play”. Why these complications are necessary?  Your designers get extra points for each frustrated user?  I don’t see any other meaningful explanation.  KISS, aka Keep it simple. 
P.s. “repeat indefinitely” still stops sound after 120min.

title: This app will eventually drive you crazy
body:
When this app works it is wonderful. The music for the different moods is a great fit.  But if you ever want to listen underground or on a plane or someplace without strong cell signal ... get ready to be angry.

To begin with, the app does not download the various music to your phone in advance. Everything is streamed. If you want to listen to anything offline you must plan in advance and guess what moods you will be in and then try to download the song tracks that you may want.  This is an unnecessary pain.  The developers could easily include at least 10% of the tracks in the app so that thousands of users will not be left with literally no tracks when we are not actively connected to the net.

And what makes it all worse is that the download process for individual tracks doesn’t seem to work at all and has not for weeks or longer.  In order to download a track you need to find it and then open it while connected and then click the download icon in the top right of the screen.

But then prepare yourself to see the icon spinning in a circle forever with no indication of whether anything is downloading or how long is left.

I have tried downloading in half a dozen locations with strong internet and it just never works.

UPDATE AUG 1, 2020 - The newest version of this app is in beta testing and I am a beta tester.  The download and listen offline feature works!  So, once the new version is released I will update my review.

title: Total focus! Please support landscape orientation
body:
The concept and execution of the musicscapes to the mood or purpose is very effective. I am using for coding and writing documentation while at home. I use noise cancelling headphones for this to block out city noise. I can work for the full 90 minutes in a very focused and productive manner. It is helping me meet deadlines, so very happy! 

I do wish that the app supported landscape mode on the iPhone and, in particular the iPad. I have the latter in a stand horizontally and having to look at the screen sideways isn’t fun.

The other observation is that the tonality of the content appear to be equalized to be bass heavy or the codec is using a lower sample rate. My headphones are reference design and this is quite noticeable compared to say iTunes content. This may be by design as psychoacoustics are probably part of the formula. After 5 minutes I don’t notice, but initially I feel compelled to adjust something. I would be interested to know if this is by design.

body:

Also, the noise is intense and doesn’t necessarily feel positive or happy, almost a negative feeling. In addition, I felt more tired throughout the day after using. But, maybe that’s because it just STOPS in the middle of an hour sleep.

title: Amazing. The best app out there
body:
This app is incredible. By far the best of all the focus / white noise / binaural beats app I’ve tried.  

I’ve been using the app daily for over a year now, and it has helped my focus and concentration immensely.  The Focus tracks on this app (-Beach Focus and Wind Focus are particularly helpful) have helped me finally get ahold of my ADD / ADHD.  With this app, I’m so much better at focusing on my most important tasks & blocking out distractions. It’s a real lifesaver for getting things done at work. 

I would agree with the other reviewers that the actual layout of the current app isn’t the best, and I think the old version of the app actually looked more polished and was more intuitive. That being said, the amazing quality of the audio tracks (and my resulting increased productivity) more than makes up for this, and I’m sure the developer will be updating the design of the actual app in the future.

body: I recently subscribed to this app on a monthly basis to help me study after enjoying the free sessions. Thanks for nothing Brain.fm. I’d like my money back.

author: Kyle 1305

title: App crashes
body:
Just got this app (paid), and on iPhone 6s (iOS 13.1.1) the app keeps freezing. Had no problem during free trial, but now ...... well it’s definitely entraining my brain and the thoughts aren’t nice.

Update Jan. 30, 2020.  No longer crashes. It is stable.  But the app seems immature relative to other music or meditation apps. Comparing it to AMZN, Spotify, Calm, Headspace.  Here is the difference: when the app is playing and a phone call comes, or if I need to launch another app that will use the speaker, I cannot return to the same place within the app; cannot pick up where I left off. Instead I need to relaunch a “song” with a different mood, unless I go back through the history to find which one I was doling, then restart it. Since I use Focus as a work timer ( to allow for breaks) it throws off the sequence.  
Second minor complaint: within the larger categories of Focus, Relax, Meditate, Sleep, there a subcategories. What do they do? For example, what is the difference between  “Chill” “Unwind” “Recharge”. I cannot seem to find anything that explains how one is different from another.  I know the science behind this is supposed to be great, but I already have music for binaural or isochronic backgrounds to support focus states, meditation, sleep, etc.  In direct comparison, Brain.fm is either equivalent or worse from subjective POV.  But if I dial-up Theta 8Hz, or Alpha/Theta isochronic sounds, at least I can subjectively note the difference with repeated use.  With Brain.fm, I cannot notice a difference within a category like “Relax”— they all seem the same.

author: toe knoee

title: The old app worked. The new app doesn’t.
body:
EDIT: Paid member. Still missing the old app, honestly. This one just cannot keep playing downloaded tracks past 30 minutes. I have to stop what I’m doing to restart the track and that completely defeats the purpose of having a concentration track on. 

Looks like these issues are fairly common. C’mon, y’all! We believe in you! I’m all for new features, but basic playback functionality should be non-negotiable.

***

Honestly, I liked the old app better. The new app is buggy, crashes, and doesn’t last longer than half an hour playing on airplane mode—making it impossible to use in a lot of contexts. This morning, it won’t even load. 

Devs, take this one back to Testflight and bring back the old design—at least until you figure out basic functionality.
author: Aldarie

title: So many issues, cannot use the app at all!
body:
2 stars is for the concept. It seriously lacks execution, listening to consumers , making updates accordingly and believing in their products (aince they refuse to reimburse a consumer’s money but keep her as a super annoyed one everytime she tries to use the app!)
I did their trial - a certain number of free sessions- which each session was cut 1/2 or 1/4 as something got in my way (i have kids) and could not pause and keep going when I’m back! But I really loved the concept and wanted to do the annual plan, only to discover within a week that 1- whenever the phone connection is bad, it doesn’t play (and the phone connection is not good in our home, we have a well working wifi but it still does not work in some rooms, ugh) I understand you can download some tracks, but I cannot foresee what I’d feel like listening and download all the tracks :/ Oh and at those same rooms, I can open the youtube app and listen to any focus music without issues 2- you have to choose one of their predetermined time limits, if you want to work for 15 mins only, you need to choose 30 mins and set a timer 3-it glitches a lot, many times I open another app, screen on my phone to check sth, the music is cut off 4-it takes a lot of time to switch between musics, and everytime I want different music option that fits my mood, I have to set up 5 min prep time before I get into focus mode.
I am sad to have wasted my money on this app, and they clearly do not care what their consumers think. Despite I sent them a mail explaining all these, they chose to act as if they did not understand immediate cancelllation and reimbursement, but gave directions on how I can stop the auto-renew process for 2021, which I had already done before contacting them! 
What a waste of a beautiful idea & a perfect example on how to  lose a customer for life!
author: NutritiousMom

title: This app is legit.
body: True story: I am an adult with ADHD and use this app to focus while working. Yesterday, I was working at Starbucks and so focused that when the dude behind me got arrested, I didn’t even notice. He was fully handcuffed in the store while I was zoning out on some emails. It’s like audio Adderall.
author: Rev. Sean Steele

title: Love the app, but..
body:
I love this app. The quality music, the design, etc. There is only one problem with this app—and it’s a big one. The actually playback of the music is very sketchy. If I use Siri, the music pauses and doesn’t continue when I’m done with Siri. If I have my messages round aloud in Messages, the music stops and doesn’t continue when I’m done. Same with dictation. It seems as though if anything interrupts the music, it doesn’t pickup where it left off. So you have to unlock your phone, go to the app, and unpause the music. For how much this cost on annual basis (not a ton more than Disney+), I would expect this basic functionality to be flawless.

Outside of the playback issues, it’s a great app with music that does what they promise.

title: Dec19 - multiple crashes
body:
As of December 19th, the app has repeatedly crashed. It’s unfortunate because it’s a great service that’s rendered inaccessible and useless since it’s new app redesign. The backend seems to be buggy. Here’s what my interaction with the app looks like these days:

I’m getting ready to work. So I click on the app, see the blue screen with their logo—crash. Repeat 3 times.

Playing songs, skip. Crash. Repeat at least twice.

Hitting skip repeats the same song and doesn’t skip sometimes.

Yup.

title: Great idea poor execution
body: The idea and research here is great, but I don’t think that the app actually helps sooth the mind. If anything, especially if you are someone young that wants to use this app, this app will only increase stress levels for you. It’s happened to all my friends and even myself who use the app. For some reason, and I don’t know exactly why, the lack of pace lulls your mind into not executing the work you are trying to do efficiently and quickly, and drags out the amount of time you have to do your work. The app also is purposely designed for you to stay on it as long as possible, as all apps are, and while that can be good, it also means that you are spending less time working and more time choosing a song you might like. I don’t see significant differences in songs from focus and meditation, to even sleep. I like the idea for this app but don’t recommend it.

title: App developers not listening to paying customers
body:
I loved this app when it first came out. It was the only one of its kind and you couldn’t beat the binaural and very unique sound quality.  I actually raved about it in an E-book I wrote for my online community. It a few updates later, and the app is actually MORE difficult to navigate, bulky, buggy and is actually worse as far as user interface is concerned. The sounds won’t change when tapped, the app crashes, the functionality is not streamlined.  I’ve left feedback and asked questions before and gotten no response.

It doesn’t seem like the changes were done with experienced beta testers, otherwise these updates would have not made sense to the experienced user who wants an app to meditate/focus/relax/sleep daily.  I am a tech-savvy woman entrepreneur in my 30’s, meditate daily and often have to sleep during odd daytime hours so I use my noise canceling earbuds with a sleep feature to keep out the noises of lawn mowers, doorbells and such.  

In my general opinion, I don’t think the app developers are listening to users. I was a paid subscriber for months, maybe almost a year, but since no app updates seemed to improve the app (and things are not getting fixed and are becoming WORSE), I will be canceling my subscription.  Such a bummer, too. Maybe I’ll invest in Pzizz.

author: MSWaddington

title: What happened?
body:
The new release is terrible,  Why? Just... why?

(Updated)

To clarify— I don’t care that you updated the user interface. I wasn’t fond of the old one. The new one has a different set of problems. Some things are better. Some aren’t. Things that used to be easy are now slow and obscure. Things I never used to do at all are suddenly encouraged and easy. So it goes. I know it’s hard to craft a UI that is simple, easy to learn, and yet reveals deeper functionality and flexibility when you need it. It’s a subjective thing, anyway. You can’t please everyone. 

What was hard to take was the surprise of suddenly not being able to use the app. No warning, no self-congratulatory, “Hey, we’ve updated the UI with these cool features” with a guided tour or something. I couldn’t figure out how to do what I’ve done easily before. It made me angry. 

I use your app to regulate attention and mood when I’m distracted, unproductive, and most of all, very stressed. Your UI designers probably already know that your customers arrive at your UI stressed and out of sorts, anxious to get their own work done and not at all prepared to have to figure out how to use your app. Or worse, learn it again. Please reflect this understanding when you change things around. The next time you make an effort to improve the UI, a little more attention to on-boarding lifetime customers like me would be appreciated. 

Having said all this, please know that, despite the UI, the sounds work. Within minutes. I also appreciate your efforts to add new sounds and new app functionality. That’s why I’m still a customer. I’m just cranky. And stressed. 

I’m gonna see if I can get your app to help me de-stress and focus like it used to.

title: Vast improvement to my sleep and study/work
body:
As to be expected, I was quite skeptical around how successful this would turn out to be. However, I am glad to report that my sleep habits have vastly improved while using this app.

I prefer the Deep Sleep over the Guided Sleep personally, mostly because I feel that I tend to focus more on the voice instead of what I’m being told to do. The Deep Sleep on the other hand puts me out hard. This is especially helpful for me as I work graveyard so sleeping in general can be a battle. This has helped a ton.

In relation to work and study. Using traditional music was always my default but I’d often get caught up in the lyrics to a song or messing with playlists thus pulling my attention away.

This tool removes that as it utilizes music that is stimulating but not in such a way that gets in front of what you’re trying to do. So far I haven’t found a “favorite” tune while working. I find this a plus since the point is focus, not music listening.

I appreciate the timing options especially during study and work as it reminds me to stop for a bit and rest, this further increasing focus when it matters.

My only complaint... It should better interact with EarPod and Beats controls. Pressing pause on the remote does not seem to do anything. Additionally, the controls are not always reliable in Control Center. I feel this is something that is likely to be addressed as it’s annoying when I’m having to fiddle with my phone to pause the music. 

Otherwise, great tool and worth the buy.

title: My go-to app
body:
(I’m amending my earlier lower star review for several reasons. Please read through.)

Brain.fm is one of the apps I use all the time. Practically every day. I use it to sleep and at work to focus. I still think it’s the best app out there for focus, but the sleep portion of the app has not been good to me lately. 

There have been some update issues with the app over the past six months or so that have rendered it very difficult to use for sleep. Connectivity problems were the biggest issue. It would often stop after anywhere from 10 minutes to 2 hours. 

Then, a little over a week or two ago, they released a major update. This update missed the mark with me completely. However, I sent feedback through the app, and the team reached out to me and actually listened to my concerns. That goes a long way for me. 

The redesign is a little jarring if you’ve used the old app for a while, but it is very easy to use, and I am hopeful that the few problems I currently have with the app (like not being able to select the specific song I want without cycling through all of the others) will be fixed with a future update. 

Above all, I want to applaud the Brain.fm team for listening to feedback and wanting to make things better for their users. 

I hope to be able to update this review again in a week or two with a glowing 5 star again. I do love the product and will highly recommend it again if the connectivity issues and a few of the UI issues are resolved.

author: TheShrewKing

title: Account / password reset needs work
body: I’ve been a loyal subscriber to Brain.fm for two years.  The music is amazing for focus, relaxation and sleep.  Zero complaints - I personally experience the value of their music and science coming together.  But...with this recent release which logged me out, the account management capabilities, especially passwords, has gone south big time.  It is a mystery now how to update and manage your password. Needs serious work.
author: singaporeflier

title: App Fail. Found better sleep option FREE
body:
After paying to use brain.fm and having the app fail 100% of the time when using it for sleep, AND trying to get a fix, I’ve now finally given up. 

I have found a much better option with an app that actually works. What a concept! It’s free and the quality of my sleep is the best result. Thanks to Relax Melodies,I finally feel rested!
author: yesitsmyrealnickname

title: Update Ruined It
body: I liked this app prior to the latest update which made it no longer free and changed the UI making it much more difficult and frustrating to navigate. Only about 1/3 of the unguided meditation “songs” I liked anyway. The others sounded like a science fiction soundtrack or had fake nature sounds. And I get that they want money from users, but I would have preferred ads over making it pay-for-play. There’s too much competition without these problems. Developers missed the mark on this one.
author: PakaLoloSwami

title: Love it, hate it
body:
The goal of this app is to put you in a relaxed/focused state. I find it is more like a flip of the coin: 50% chance of a trouble-free stream, 50% of frustration at trying to get it to work.
When it works, I love it. However, it often disappoints me as well.
I mostly use the app for focus in the office, and when it works I find it extremely helpful. The problem is that the app, through multiple updates, has had playback issues. I eventually gave up on live streaming, and simply downloaded a few streams and relied on Offline mode. The latest update deleted my offline downloads, and would not stream through an entire session. So, I downloaded a stream, put the device in Airplane mode, and now it will not play...
author: Sasane

title: Log in errors
body: There are a lot of log in errors here. L Every time I close the app, I get logged out, then my password won’t work. If I delete app and download again, then the same password will suddenly work. I have to do this process every day.
author: ftdertghu

title: Great sounds, terrible app
body:
Something’s really broken about how this app is coded. I’ve had it for years, and connectivity issues are constant. Find a sound you like? Download it. And never change. Because streaming anything may stop. Pause it? It won’t resume. Skip track? Maybe it’ll work, if you’re lucky.
With the update, now it’s not recognizing my login half the time. The fix? From the help people? Erase and reinstall the app. I’ve done that three times tonight. When it does work, it’s got a shiny new coat of UI—but it’s still hard to navigate. Change your mind about which sleep category you want? Good luck backing out! Oh, and a TINY problem remains: it still loses connection when downloading a track, won’t advance tracks, freezes, forces a new logins... which don’t work, requiring erasure and reinstalling. 
The core product is SOLID, but this app needs to be rewritten from the ground up by someone who knows what they’re doing.
author: Jorsin

title: Brain.fm is my #1 work secret
body: I get so much done when I listen to the focus music, it’s insane. A total staple in my workflow. And the new app update is AWESOME! So functional and robust, really improved UI/UX. Just want to say a big thanks to the hardworking team for bringing us all this amazing service and being tireless about constantly improving it and providing stellar support! I’m a fan for life and I tell everyone who will listen to me about how awesome Brain.fm is - not only in mission, but in actual, proven effectiveness. I get into such crazy flow when I pop on my favorite focus tracks. For a freelance designer who sometimes finds it difficult to ‘just get started’ on overwhelming/demanding creative tasks, Brain.fm has become simply essential in my daily routine. Thank you, thank you, thank you 🙏🏻
author: sarahbrown2357

title: WAS amazing...now, not so much.
body: I’ve had Brain FM for about a year now and loved it, except for the random times it would stop playing in the middle of the night. But after the update, I’m not a fan. My husband and I always played the ocean/beach waves and it played the same sound throughout the night. Now, we start off our sleep with the ocean serenity station and it plays other sounds that make us wake up. Really disappointed that we can’t just choose one sound to listen to compared to a “station” of different similar sounds. Will be finding another app now.
author: tdiedz

title: Go within (and go back to the previous version)
body:
The new purplish, smiley faces version of the app takes away the benefits of entrainment. Functions and layout are counterintuitive. Aesthetically unpleasant. 
I also shouldn’t have to login back in constantly, especially when it won’t recognize my login and I have to delete the app and reinstall.
Please go back to the previous version. Simplicity is the key. The content is fantastic. Makes sure we can access it better.
Thanks.

author: Tung (Tom)

title: Not a good showing, folks.
body:

New UI is bad and unintuitive. Please restore the user controls you had before. 

Also, lost all my offline tracks previously saved, and had to listen to someone talking to me about an app I’ve used for years and to which I bought a lifetime subscription.

Edit: Thanks for the response, but I still maintain the ability to pick tracks is missing. If I deselect everything under Mood except Grooves, I don’t get Grooves tracks. At least not the ones I got before that I saved for offline use. I want to actively pick tracks, especially the ones I use most often. The old version also had more choices overall.

I like to listen to music while I work but nothing that distracts me from what I’m working on which makes this perfect.

title: Love the app (with only one caveat)
body:
I use Brain.fm both for focusing and relaxing, and I’ve been exceptionally happy with it on both counts.

The one caveat: the most recent overhaul that went live in the last week added a lot of great features (love the subcategories under Focus), but also took away a vital feature — the ability to stop whatever category of music you’re in and choose another (say, switch from multi-task to creative, or focus to relax). 

Now, once you start listening to a particular kind of music, the only way to switch to a different one is to close the app, reopen it and then choose the new type. Especially frustrating since the new subcategories makes the idea of jumping from one to another as you change what type of work you’re doing over the course of the day very appealing.

title: Great App
body:
Just wanted to say that so far I’m really enjoying the app but thought I’d give you a suggestion that might help to improve the user experience and even get more sales from the trial period. 

- At first glance it’s not apparent that there are multiple selections for each category. Therefore having some type of menu enabling the user to see the different choices would both give a user an idea of the number of choices available but also enable a user to easily return to a previous selection without having to press the skip button over and over until the desired selection is found and recognized. 

Perhaps an option to save favorites would be good too!
author: dwhit16

title: Instant calm
body:
I love this app. It immediately puts me into a meditative state and absolutely clears my mind. 
I have ADHD, PTSD, and severe anxiety; I am very easily overwhelmed, and my brain almost never turns off. With this app, it’s like finally feeling that relaxing, floaty clarity. 
The visualizations that come to me are both fleeting and vivid. Bright colors, clear faces and objects. Feels almost as though I’m tapping into a sixth sense. Not dreaming, because I’m not asleep- possibly hypnotized, and able to receive whatever comes to me. 
I have never experienced anything like it- and I thoroughly appreciate that my mind, for once, isn’t swarming with stress.

title: Great App

author: seanb2131

title: Awesome ADHD focus, new music needed
body: I’ve used the app for well over a year almost everyday. I am severe ADHD and the music helps me focus in ways I’ve not ever found before. Incredible, seriously. But I have listened to every track about 25 times. There just aren’t that many. Devs - any new music in the pipeline?
author: bradley-g

title: Do the devs even use the app??
body:
I love brain.fm. It’s just such a shame that the app is horrible and has remained horrible for as long as I can remember.

Issue 1:
Connectivity issues.
The app doesn’t know the phone is connected to the internet. Often when switching to a different mode, from relax to focus for example, the app throws an error saying that it isn’t connected to the internet. I can swap over to a ping test or speed test and confirm there is no issue with my network connection. Swap back and it will never reconnect and keeps say there is no internet. The only way to fix is to quit out of the app and relaunch it. 

Issue 2:
Offline saving doesn’t work. 
I used to have a bunch saved for offline listening to avoid Issue 1. Then they all started to get corrupted. Since then I haven’t been able to listen to any offline or even create any. 2 phones later and the issue hasn’t been fixed. 

Issue 3:
Contacting support is a joke. 
I was a day late on purchasing a lifetime license, the deadline came and they were no longer selling them. (I had been saving for a long time because it was quite expensive) I contact them and they play hard ball and say to just pay a subscription. Yeah a subscription that’s nearly the cost of a lifetime license and will quickly out scale that. Sure I’d pay a subscription if the devs fixed the app and created new content and features. I’d pay a subscription to have good support that wasn’t so rude. But here we are and none of that exists. I’m sorry to say that I wasted all the money I saved up for a lifetime license on a subscription. 

I won’t be renewing or recommending this to anyone until all of the above has been addressed and fixed to my satisfaction.
author: ManjaroBlack

title: Still buggy years later
body:
Software is great, but app is plagued with bugs. Latest one is the continual pausing of playback. Previously, offline tracks would not play correctly (if I selected an 8 hr sleep track it would stop after 45 mins if I had also downloaded a nap track).

I’ve shared this feedback with the team numerous times, and have tried to be patient as they worked through the bugs. 2+ years is plenty of time to figure this out.
author: CJSF2323

title: Terrible customer service
body: I upgraded for the pro version within the app and the upgrade didn’t happen. I was logged out, and when logged back in I was still on the free version. I contacted the customer service immediately. It’s been almost a week, several emails and my issue isn’t fixed! I email, they reply asking for the app store receipt, I send and then no reply. It’s been twice already. I feel really frustrated because I paid $50 can’t even get a refund. When trying to report the problem to Apple, who charged my card through my apple id account, and automatic response says my problem doesn’t qualify for refund and all other options tell me to contact the app.
author: LeoZaratustra

title: Nice app but needs improvement
body:
I like this app's simplicity. You don't have to make a lot of decisions- you just pick a category and nice music starts playing. You do have limited options for your timer, though. 

The worst part is that the app is very buggy. The sleep app would make it through the entire night about one out of ten times. It usually cut out quickly. I emailed support about this. They told me to reinstall the app. I told them I did this, but it didn't improve. They never replied again. 

Sometimes, the app would also say that my wife wasn't working. But, everything else on my phone and computer was running smoothly on my home's wifi. 

I was a subscriber for about 3 months. But, I ended up finding a much better app with many more options for the same price.

author: FossilizedCarlos

title: Pretty... but creepy?
body: It’s a little unnerving, they seemingly use the same three frequencies and oscillations for every track in it’s category. And it’s not subtle, even on low you can hear the oscillating over whichever track is playing. I’ve listened to frequency and ambient music for years and I’ve never quite felt in-a-twilight-zone-elevator-quietly-drifting-through-an-endless-void like I do with these tracks. They do however have a luxurious feel to them. The sound quality is really clean and soft and you can really feel it surround you. That aspect is what’s relaxing. It feels a little like you’re being pampered -as long as you don’t think too hard about what you’re hearing. As far as focus goes, I feel not much different and I’ve been listening for almost an hour. I feel... somewhat disturbed, as if something bads about to happen. It’s sometimes got an almost impending-doom feel, like dystopia in a crystal clean glass mansion. Good stuff guys, i’ll keep it.

title: Suggestions 😁😁

body: I’ve been using this app for several weeks now and see a marked increase in my productivity at work when I use it. title: Meditation, Sleep and Focus App
body:
I discovered this app when I began using a Muse headband to train myself to relax and to calm my active brain.  I’ve been pleasantly surprised at how quickly I’ve been able to get to a calm state.  My ultimate goal was to hear the voice of GOD speaking to me. I know HE is always communicating with us but we have to learn to still and quiet our mind to hear HIS Still Small Voice.  When we learn to listen and actually have an experience with HIM, we are truly blessed with an experience that is indescribable.  Words cannot begin to describe the euphoric feeling I’ve experienced in feeling the presence of GOD.  I wish the whole entire human civilization could experience this peace that “surpasses all understanding”.  

I’ve rated this app 5 stars because I have used it for sleep which was very effective and for Focus also.  In using the sounds and music, I have been able to tune out the world (with use of headphones) and use the the app as it was intended, i.e. sleep, meditation, focus, etc.  I have found it very useful and effective.  I highly recommend this app along with using the app to monitor brain waves which gives visual confirmation to the level of calm I experience.

I’ve reached out multiple times about this and never got a response. Very close to asking for a refund for my subscription.

title: Been life changing for me
body:
I love this app. I’ve been using it consistently for over 2 years.

The focus one totally kicks in for me hard at about 5 minutes. 

The relax one puts me in a meditative state within a few mins. 

And the sleep one is incredibly effective for me. I use that one the most. 

Few feedback points though:
- the streaming feature is kinda weird so I just click the download option and listen right off the app on my phone instead of the internet.

- I wish there was an ergonomic earbud headphone they sold cause my ears can get slightly sore after awhile but it’s not enough for me to not use it. It’s like Pavlov’s Dogs. The soundtrack knocks me out very quickly which can be hard naturally for my over active brain. 

Overall, I can’t recommend this app and subscription enough. The benefits massively outweigh any minor annoyance.

title: Unfortunate service for a great app
body:

I emailed customer service who charged me on Jan 8th without my authorization. I replied on Jan 9th and again on Jan 16th, requesting that I hear from them no later then Jan 18th. It's now the 27th and I haven't heard anything. After failed email attempts I sent them a DM on Instagram. Nothing.

To add insult to injury, the app continues to tell me I'm out of free trial plays when I paid for a 3 month subscription 3 weeks ago.

body:

My only recommendation is to allow pause/play functionality with connected headphones and develop more of a workout based playlist (thinking of Terminator movie them sounds, drums, clanging metal, inspirational stuff).

title: Fantastic for Focus and Sleep Alike
body:
I’m extremely happy I found this app. I used to just use calming songs through Apple Music to study with my noise cancelling headphones, but since downloading this app, for studying I largely don’t use anything else. I never realized how much background playlists like “nightsounds” and “thunder” helped until I had the chance to use it. It’s extremely less distracting than music (which I would usually need to play quietly) and generally seems to perform better at keeping me focused (I can keep the volume higher so noise cancelling is more effective). 

But not only that, the “recharge” playlist is super useful for times where you know you need a nap (as it’d be beneficial) but you just can’t get comfortable enough or relaxed enough to sleep (or at least it’s helpful for me). 

The only thing I wish is that all of the playlists had options for unlimited streaming (no timer) rather than mandatorily needing to choose a timer only to have to restart the playlist again when the timer runs out. This is a tad bit frustrating, as it’s rather abrupt to suddenly have the streaming end when one isn’t expecting it. But, overall, it’s not a dealbreaker. 

Overall, worth the download and purchase of the subscription, and I’m glad I found this app.
